new_findings: NARA's official UAP bulk-download page confirms stable series 595466 and 597821 and exposes separate metadata objects for each series.
The NARA public page confirms individual Blue Book case files are chronologically arranged and have date/location finding aids/microfilm access, making a date-first reference request appropriate.
The current execution environment could not directly decode the NARA bulk JSON/ZIP MIME object; no attempt was made to infer an item identifier from that technical limitation.
Case 4810 / NARA-PBB1-167 remains a nonofficial locator hint only.
Historical Navy Operations and Readiness schedule N1-NU-89-005 predates the 2004 event and explicitly lists SSIC 3560 Combat Information Center Logs with a three-year disposition.
The same historical schedule contains SSIC 3610-3613 Electronic Warfare/ESM/ECM/ECCM record families with permanent primary-program records but shorter-lived routine/general records.
NARA's current notice states that most remaining items from N1-NU-89-005 were later superseded by DAA-NU-2015-0003; that successor schedule was approved in 2018.
This makes finite operational-record retention a historically contemporaneous plausible mechanism around 2004, not merely a post-2010 analogy.
No public source found in R5 maps Princeton AN/SPY-1 raw returns themselves to SSIC 3560 or 361x, so destruction of the specific radar data is NOT established.
NARA confirms that the 1973-1979 Central Foreign Policy File was indexed electronically, with most telegrams electronic and hard-copy documents on microfilm/P-Reels but electronically indexed.
NARA identifies the CFPF series as NAID 654098 with electronic telegram and index files, supporting date/message-based retrieval rather than generic subject browsing.

DIA's public primary message remains the event-level measurement narrative; DIA FOIA logs show multiple later requests specifically targeting the 19 September 1976 Tehran F-4 incident, confirming a formal retrieval lineage but not additional telemetry.
No new F-4 radar tape, maintenance/fault log, or Mehrabad ground-radar record was recovered in public indexed surfaces in R5.
